title: POC planning: Open-model shortlist & multilingual eval — Bridgepoint Analytics
summary: Kickoff/POC scoping for a 4-week evaluation of open models for multilingual financial-extractive tasks. Discussed shortlist (Llama-3 variants, Mistral, Mosaic), quality vs latency/cost tradeoffs, dataset language coverage (EN, ES, PT, FR), success criteria (F1/precision targets and latency SLOs), bench plan and responsibilities. Action: Redwood to share security pack and test plan; Bridgepoint to share sample dataset and target prompts; schedule dedicated benchmark run.
next_steps: Maya to send SOC2 + security pack and private deployment checklist by 2028-02-12
Bridgepoint to drop anonymized sample dataset (10k docs, multilingual) into shared S3 by 2028-02-13
Schedule 1-hour benchmark run on Redwood Dedicated for 2028-02-20 (Ethan to own)
Follow-up sync 2028-02-23 to review initial results and decide shortlist

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-02-09 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Rosa (Redwood SE), Lena, Owen, Priya, Markus (Bridgepoint)

Summary: Kickoff POC: Bridgepoint wants to explore open-model options for multilingual information extraction from financial reports and earnings transcripts. Focus on precision for entity extraction, low-latency inference for an online pipeline, and European language coverage (English, Spanish, Portuguese, French).

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Maya, AE on the account, and with me are Ethan and Rosa from engineering. How's everybody?
00:14 Lena: Hi thanks, Lena here. We're excited.
00:18 Owen: Owen, platform team; we've got the infra questions.
00:22 Priya: Priya, PM here.
00:27 Maya: Great. The goal for today is to nail down what success looks like for the POC, the workload sizing, and a realistic bench plan. Also we'll propose a shortlist of open models to try.
00:36 Markus: Quick context — we run nightly ingest of earnings calls and then do extraction for KPIs; latency matters for interactive dashboards. We're also expanding into LATAM markets so Spanish and Portuguese are priorities.
00:50 Ethan: Understood. A couple of clarifying Qs: what's your expected qps for interactive use versus batch reprocessing?
00:58 Markus: For interactive dashboards it's small — like 10 to 20 concurrent users, but each user can trigger 2-3 requests per minute during heavy periods. Batch reprocessing is more throughput intensive, 200-400 rps over a few hours.
01:16 Rosa: That's helpful. For the POC we typically run two bench modes: a 1-hour interactive simulation to exercise tail latencies and a larger batch pass to measure throughput and unit cost.
01:28 Priya: Good. What about success metrics? We care about extraction F1, false positive rate, and also cost per 1000 tokens.
01:36 Maya: Would it make sense to set numeric targets now? For example: extraction F1 >= 0.82 on your gold set, precision >= 0.85 for financial entities, p95 latency < 300ms for the interactive workload, and cost per 1k tokens below your internal threshold. Is that reasonable?
01:51 Lena: That sounds reasonable as a starting point. We may tighten precision for certain entities like revenue vs generic metrics.
01:58 Ethan: On the models side we propose a shortlist: Llama-3 13B finetuned variant, Mistral-Instruct 7B, MosaicML MPT-7B-instruct, and a quantized 13B from a community release. We also recommend testing a multilingual-specific variant — e.g., Llama 3 + multilang fine-tune or a specialized polyglot model.
02:18 Markus: Any thoughts on Hugging Face Infinity / Anthropic-like performance?
02:23 Ethan: Competitors offer good latency in some configs but the tradeoffs are control and data residency. With Redwood Dedicated you get reserved capacity and VPC options which helps. Also our runtime supports prefix/KV caching and batching strategies that materially lower per-token cost for repeated prompts.
02:41 Owen: About caching — if we have repeated prefixes (like company name, instruction prompt), how much hit do we expect?
02:47 Rosa: In our experience prefix/KV caching can shave 30-60% of compute for repeated context depending on cache hit rates. It depends on how much of the prompt is stable vs fresh text.
02:59 Lena: Is quantization on the table? We're very cost conscious.
03:03 Ethan: Yes, int8/QLoRA style quantization helps. For some 13B variants you can run 8-bit kernels with small accuracy drops — often <3% delta in F1 for extraction tasks, varies by model. We'll include both FP16 and int8 runs in the bench.
03:22 Priya: For languages like Portuguese, we historically saw performance drop-offs — do you have multilingual model benchmarks?
03:28 Maya: We don't have Bridgepoint-specific numbers yet, so the POC will include language-sliced metrics. We'll measure recall/precision per language and per entity class.
03:37 Owen: Regarding security — do you support customer-managed KMS and SSO? We need RBAC and audit logs for compliance.
03:44 Maya: Yes, Redwood Private and Dedicated support KMS integration and audit logs. We'll send the SOC2 report and the KMS doc. For SSO we do SAML and OIDC SSO, and RBAC is configurable.
03:56 Lena: Good. Also need data residency — some EU data must stay in eu-central.
04:01 Rosa: We can pin region and run workloads in eu-central with Dedicated. That will be part of the deployment spec.
04:09 Ethan: On sizing — given your numbers, for interactive at 20 users peak with concurrency and latency SLOs, we'd recommend reserving a small pool of A100-equivalent or 1-2 x H100-like nodes depending on model choice; for batch, autoscale to a larger pool for throughput bursts. We'll provide a cost estimate for each model's footprint.
04:32 Markus: Can you give an example of expected p50/p95 with the Mistral 7B vs Llama-3 13B?
04:38 Ethan: Rough ballpark: Mistral 7B on our infra often hits p50 ~60-80ms, p95 ~180-250ms for single-stream tokens at typical seq lengths; Llama-3 13B FP16 might be p50 ~120-150ms, p95 ~300-400ms unless quantized and batched. But accuracy tradeoffs may favor the 13B for specialized financial language.
05:00 Priya: For bench we need to measure both native generation latency and total end-to-end extraction time (tokenize+postprocess).
05:07 Rosa: We'll include tokenization time in the harness; we'll also surface end-to-end metrics with your extraction pipeline.
05:13 Lena: What's a realistic POC timeline?
05:17 Maya: We recommend a four-week cadence: week 0 (this week) alignment and data ingestion, week 1 integration + small smoke bench, week 2 full benchmark runs across the shortlist, week 3 iterate on top-2 models and test quantization + caching, week 4 final report and decision.
05:33 Priya: That aligns with our Q1 goals. Who signs off at the end?
05:36 Lena: Myself and the head of data products — they'll evaluate technical metrics plus infra cost estimates.
05:41 Ethan: About bench specifics — we'll run quality metrics (F1/precision/recall per entity and per language), latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput (rps), and cost per 1k tokens. We'll also report on model stability (variance across runs) and failure modes.
05:57 Markus: For quality tests, do you do prompt ensembles or multiple prompting strategies?
06:02 Rosa: Yes, we'll try direct instruction prompts, few-shot examples, and a light chain-of-thought style prompt for ambiguous extractions. We'll keep the prompt template consistent across models for fair comparison.
06:16 Lena: How do you handle hallucinations on numeric values — a big worry for finance?
06:20 Ethan: We'll add numeric verification steps in the pipeline, but fundamentally model choice and temperature matter. We'll benchmark at temperature 0 and 0.2 for comparison. Also using constrained decoding or classification-based extraction for fields that must be exact can help.
06:36 Priya: Any concerns about legal/procurement? We may need an NDA amendment for sample data.
06:40 Maya: If needed we can execute a short addendum; I'll coordinate legal.
06:44 Markus: Regarding observability, can we see token-level cost breakdowns?
06:47 Rosa: Yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level cost and latency per route/model, and we can add tracing hooks to your pipeline.
06:55 Owen: For the benchmark harness, we'll want to simulate both single-user interactive traffic and a batch pass.
06:59 Ethan: We'll provide the harness as a runnable script and a small runner that you can trigger in your account. For Dedicated we can spin up the reserved nodes and run the harness under your VPC.
07:12 Priya: Is there any pre-existing integration work on our side we should plan for?
07:15 Owen: We'll need to open some network egress and allow the Redwood endpoints, and create IAM role for S3. We'll also coordinate region settings.
07:24 Maya: Ok, recap and next steps — I'll list them and then we can confirm: "1) Maya to send security pack and SOC2 by Feb 12; 2) Bridgepoint to provide anonymized sample dataset (10k docs) by Feb 13; 3) Ethan to prepare benchmark harness and cost estimates by Feb 18; 4) Schedule benchmark run Feb 20; 5) Follow-up on Feb 23." Any amendments?
07:44 Lena: Sounds good. Add Rosa as the engineering contact for the run.
07:48 Maya: Noted. Anything else?
07:50 Markus: One ask — can you include a test of multilingual fine-tuned variant vs base multilingual model?
07:55 Ethan: Yes, we'll include base multilingual models and a small fine-tune (if you can provide labels) as an optional run.
08:02 Priya: Great. Thanks everyone.
08:05 Maya: Thanks all — we'll send the pack and calendar invites after the call.
08:09 Lena: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional speaker overlap and a few mis-heard product names ("Redood" instead of Redwood) — please refer to action items for exact owners.
